history.summary: Ancient hilltop Shiva temple on a ~250-ft rocky hill in Hosur (Sanasandiram area), with panoramic views over the city. 'Chandra Choodeswarar' means the Eshwara who wears the Moon (Chandra) as the ornament on his crest; the consort is Maragathambal ('green mother' - Maragatham = green, referring to the sustaining green of plant life). 11th-century Chola stone inscriptions record donations in the reigns of Raja Raja Chola I and Kulothunga Chola I; the temple was expanded by the Hoysala king Tirubhuvanamalla Parvatharaja Anthiyazhvhar in 1260 and later came under Vijayanagara rule; it was renovated by Azakiya Perumal Aathimoolam. In Chola times Hosur was known as 'Murasu Nadu'; the name Hosur dates from the 16th century. The temple is built of soapstone with a seven-tiered rajagopuram and reportedly 103 carved sculptures. Maintained by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of Tamil Nadu. (flag) CSV 'state' column wrongly reads 'Hosur' - corrected to Tamil Nadu.

name: Chandra Choodeswarar Temple
town_description: Hosur is an industrial city in Krishnagiri district of northern Tamil Nadu on NH 44, about 40 km southeast of Bengaluru. It grew around a fort town with Chola and Hoysala history and is today a major manufacturing hub; it also draws pilgrims and day-trippers from Bengaluru to its hilltop Chandra Choodeswarar temple.

travel.railway: Hosur Railway Station (HSRA), ~3-4 km from the hill
travel.road: On NH 44 (Bangalore-Chennai highway); a motorable ghat road plus 108 steps reach the hilltop temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; the annual car festival in March-April draws the largest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 6:30 AM-12:30 PM and 4:30 PM-8:00 PM by travel sites (verify - listings vary)
